contentHtml:
beef short rib ragu simmers low and slow until the beef turns fork-tender and luxuriates in a bright tomato sauce with sautéed onions, garlic, and carrots. A hint of smoky paprika and a splash of rich beef broth deepen the flavor, while a whisper of balsamic adds lift. Tumble ribbons of pasta through the sauce so every strand gets glossy and rich. Serve for late-night laughter or next-day leftovers that taste even better. From the first aroma to the last spoonful, beef short rib ragu brings cozy warmth, big flavor, and repeat requests.

Why You’ll Love This beef short rib ragu

  • Rich, deep flavors that warm your soul.
  • Fall-off-the-bone tenderness that melts in your mouth.
  • Perfect for cozy family dinners or special occasions.
  • Easy to make with simple, wholesome ingredients.
  • Versatile dish that pairs beautifully with pasta, polenta, or crusty bread.

beef short rib ragu

Discover the ultimate comfort food with our slow-cooked beef short rib ragu recipe! Tender, flavorful, and perfect for any occasion. 🍽️✨
Print Recipe Pin Recipe
Prep Time 20 minutes mins
Cook Time 3 hours hrs
resting 10 minutes mins
Total Time 3 hours hrs 30 minutes mins
Servings: 6 servings
Course: Main Course
Cuisine: Italian
Calories: 450
Ingredients Equipment Method Notes

Ingredients
  

Main Ingredients
  • 2 lbs beef short ribs for rich flavor and tenderness
  • 2 tbsp olive oil for sautéing
  • 1 large onion, diced adds sweetness
  • 2 medium carrots, diced for a hint of sweetness
  • 2 stalks celery, diced adds depth
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced for aromatic flavor
  • 2 tbsp tomato paste intensifies tomato flavor
  • 1 cup non-alcoholic red wine or use additional beef broth as a substitute
  • 1 can (28 oz) crushed tomatoes base of the ragu
  • 2 cups beef broth for moisture
  • 2 leaves bay leaves adds fragrance
  • 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves for herbal notes
  • 1 sprig fresh rosemary complementary flavor
  • to taste salt and pepper to season
  • to garnish fresh parsley, chopped for garnish
  • as needed pasta or polenta for serving

Equipment

  • 1 Dutch oven For searing and cooking the ragu

Method
 

Preparation Steps
  1. Preheat your oven to 325°F (160°C). This will ensure your ragu cooks evenly and becomes tender.
  2. Generously season the short ribs with salt and pepper. This will enhance the flavor of the meat.
  3. Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the short ribs on all sides until they are beautifully browned. Remove them and set aside.
  4. Add chopped onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. This will create a flavorful base for your ragu.
  5. Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1–2 minutes until fragrant. Your kitchen will smell amazing!
  6. Pour in vegetable broth to deglaze, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. This adds depth to your sauce.
  7. Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, bay leaves, thyme, and rosemary. Stir well to combine all the flavors.
  8. Return the seared short ribs to the pot. Cover and transfer to the oven. Let it bake for 2½–3 hours until the meat is tender and falls off the bone.
  9. Once done, remove the short ribs from the pot. Shred the meat with two forks and discard the bones. This is where the magic happens!
  10. Stir the shredded meat back into the sauce. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Your ragu is almost ready!
  11. Serve the beef short rib ragu over pasta or polenta. Garnish with chopped parsley for a fresh touch. Enjoy your delicious creation!

How to Make Beef Short Rib Ragu

This hearty beef short rib ragu is perfect for a cozy dinner. With a preparation time of 20 minutes and a cooking time of 2½ to 3 hours, you’ll have a delicious meal ready to impress. Just let it rest for a few minutes before serving!

Step 1: Preheat the Oven

Preheat your oven to 325°F (160°C). This will ensure your ragu cooks evenly and becomes tender.

Step 2: Season the Short Ribs

Generously season the short ribs with salt and pepper. This will enhance the flavor of the meat.

Step 3: Sear the Short Ribs

Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the short ribs on all sides until they are beautifully browned. Remove them and set aside.

Step 4: Cook the Vegetables

Add chopped onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. This will create a flavorful base for your ragu.

Step 5: Add Garlic and Tomato Paste

Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1–2 minutes until fragrant. Your kitchen will smell amazing!

Step 6: Deglaze the Pot

Pour in vegetable broth to deglaze, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. This adds depth to your sauce.

Step 7: Add Remaining Ingredients

Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, bay leaves, thyme, and rosemary. Stir well to combine all the flavors.

Step 8: Return Short Ribs to the Pot

Return the seared short ribs to the pot. Cover and transfer to the oven. Let it bake for 2½–3 hours until the meat is tender and falls off the bone.

Step 9: Shred the Meat

Once done, remove the short ribs from the pot. Shred the meat with two forks and discard the bones. This is where the magic happens!

Step 10: Combine and Season

Stir the shredded meat back into the sauce. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Your ragu is almost ready!

Step 11: Serve and Enjoy

Serve the beef short rib ragu over pasta or polenta. Garnish with chopped parsley for a fresh touch. Enjoy your delicious creation!

Recipe Snapshot

Pro Tips for Making beef short rib ragu

  • Choose well-marbled beef short ribs for maximum flavor and tenderness.
  • Brown the meat thoroughly for a rich, deep flavor base.
  • Use low-sodium beef broth instead of wine for a savory depth.
  • Let the ragu simmer low and slow for at least 3 hours to develop the best taste.
  • Serve over freshly cooked pasta or creamy polenta for a comforting meal.

How to Serve this beef short rib ragu

  • Serve over creamy polenta for a comforting meal.
  • Pair with fresh tagliatelle or pappardelle pasta for a classic touch.
  • Top with grated Parmesan and fresh basil for added flavor.
  • Enjoy with crusty bread to soak up the delicious sauce.
  • Serve alongside a simple arugula salad for a fresh contrast.
  • Use as a filling for hearty sandwiches or sliders.

Make Ahead and Storage

You can prepare and store your beef short rib ragu for later enjoyment:

Storing Leftovers

  • Allow the ragu to cool completely before storing.
  • Transfer to an airtight container.
  • Refrigerate for up to 3 days.
  • Label the container with the date for easy tracking.

Freezing

  • Cool the ragu completely before freezing.
  • Use freezer-safe containers or heavy-duty freezer bags.
  • Leave some space for expansion when sealing.
  • Freeze for up to 3 months for best quality.

Reheating

  • Thaw overnight in the refrigerator if frozen.
  • Reheat on the stovetop over low heat, stirring occasionally.
  • Add a splash of broth or water if it’s too thick.
  • Ensure it’s heated through before serving.

FAQs

Here’s a helpful FAQ about this recipe:

1. What cut of beef short ribs is best for making a tender ragu?

For a tender beef short rib ragu, look for well-marbled beef short ribs. The marbling helps to keep the meat juicy and flavorful as it cooks down. Flanken-style ribs or English-style ribs are both excellent choices, as they break down beautifully during the slow cooking process, resulting in a rich and satisfying sauce.

2. How long should I braise beef short rib ragu for optimal flavor?

For optimal flavor, you should braise the beef short rib ragu for at least 3 to 4 hours. This slow cooking allows the meat to become incredibly tender and allows the flavors to meld beautifully. If you have the time, braising it for up to 6 hours can enhance the depth of flavor even further, making it a truly comforting dish.

3. Can I make beef short rib ragu in a slow cooker or Instant Pot?

Absolutely! You can make beef short rib ragu in both a slow cooker and an Instant Pot. For a slow cooker, cook on low for 6 to 8 hours or on high for 4 to 5 hours. If using an Instant Pot, you can sauté the ingredients first, then pressure cook for about 45 minutes, followed by a natural release for the best results. Both methods will yield delicious results!

4. What are the best pasta or side dishes to serve with beef short rib ragu?

Beef short rib ragu pairs wonderfully with a variety of pasta shapes, such as pappardelle, tagliatelle, or even rigatoni, as they hold the sauce well. If you prefer a lighter option, serve it over creamy polenta or mashed potatoes. A simple green salad or roasted vegetables on the side can also complement the richness of the ragu beautifully.

Final Thoughts

There you have it, a delightful Beef Short Rib Ragu that’s as comforting as a warm hug! This dish is not just simple to make, but it’s also a celebration of flavors that will have everyone asking for seconds. So roll up your sleeves, savor the process, and enjoy every delicious bite with loved ones. Happy cooking!
